\n

Doc Sync

\n

A small document app with a durable SQLite sync queue. Documents are edited locally,\n queued for sync, and pushed to an upstream service by a separate background worker.

\n
\n\n
\n

Documents (local store)

\n
    \n
  • POSTPOST /documents \u2014 create or update a document by\n slug. Creating returns 201; updating an existing slug bumps its\n version and returns 200.
    • \n
  • GETGET /documents/{slug} \u2014 read a document, including its current\n sync_status. Unknown slugs return 404.
    • \n
\n
\n\n
\n

Queueing and polling sync jobs

\n
    \n
  • POSTPOST /sync-jobs \u2014 queue a sync for the document's current version.\n The same idempotency_key always returns the original job, and an equivalent job that is already\n queued, running, or succeeded for that version is deduped instead of duplicated.
    • \n
  • GETGET /sync-jobs/{job_id} \u2014 poll a job. The payload carries\n status (queued, running, succeeded, failed,\n or conflict), the attempts counter, and any last error.
    • \n
\n
\n\n
\n

How the worker handles queued jobs

\n

A separate worker process (python worker.py --drain) claims queued jobs from SQLite, marks them\n running, and POSTs slug, title, content, and version to the\n upstream service. It never holds a database write lock across that HTTP call.

\n
    \n
  • Retry behavior: transient upstream failures (HTTP 5xx or connection errors) re-queue the same\n job row and increase its attempts counter \u2014 no duplicate jobs are created. After a bounded number\n of attempts the job is marked failed.
    • \n
  • Conflict outcomes: if the document changes after a job was queued but before it syncs, that job\n finishes with status conflict instead of pushing stale content. If a worker crashes and leaves a job\n stuck in running, a later worker run reclaims the stale job and finishes it.
    • \n
\n
\n\n
\n

Admin audit (requires X-Admin-Token)

\n
    \n
  • GETGET /admin/sync-jobs \u2014 list jobs with pagination and filters:\n ?status=succeeded&slug=launch-plan&page=1&page_size=20.
    • \n
  • GETGET /admin/sync-jobs/{job_id}/history \u2014 newest-first audit trail for a job:\n queued, started, retry, succeeded/failed,\n conflict, and reclaimed events.
    • \n
\n
\n\n

State lives in SQLite (SYNC_DB), so jobs survive restarts of both the API and the worker.
